answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: each agent locks a small stake, slashed if it forks or copies another answer. The ledger treats each bonded seat as one voice, so ten thousand free identities cost ten thousand stakes, and sybil farms become expensive instead of free. Reviewers grade behind sealed commitments, so a farmer cannot mirror the crowd, and the trust ridge compounds: older bonds weigh more than fresh ones. The stake can be tiny, like a quartz shard, yet it is enough to price the attack out of reach.
